source.title: PolyPythias: Stability and Outliers across Fifty Language Model Pre-Training Runs
source.citation: Oskar van der Wal et al., 2025
source.authors: Oskar van der Wal; Pietro Lesci; Max Müller-Eberstein; Naomi Saphra; Hailey Schoelkopf; Willem H. Zuidema; Stella Biderman

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: It compares downstream task accuracy across model sizes and training checkpoints, a different measure from held-out pretraining loss. This bears on V6, but it does not fit or test the original held-out-loss power laws or compute-optimal allocation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream accuracies across sizes and training checkpoints in Figures 1 and 6, with medians and interquartile ranges across seeds. It also plots training loss for two 410M outlier runs in Figure 5 and describes loss spikes. It does not report held-out-loss scaling fits, extrapolation tests, or a compute-optimal parameter/token split. The Chinchilla token count is cited as a reference, not tested as a loss optimum.
record.test_reason: A multi-seed stability study of Pythia 14M–410M. It reports downstream accuracy across model sizes and training checkpoints (Fig. 1, Fig. 6), which bears on V6 in a new setting: variation across seeds. The comparison is descriptive. No scaling law is fitted, and accuracy is not related to pretraining loss. Held-out-loss laws, extrapolation, allocation, shape and fit choices are not examined.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is mostly right, with refinements. The authors conclude that pretraining is largely stable across seeds and sizes. Downstream performance 'follows predictable scaling laws', which is asserted, not fitted. They find consistent learning phases (10^3–10^4 and 10^4–10^5 steps). Only two outlier runs exist (410M seeds 3 and 4), and these are detectable via training maps, which also transfer across sizes.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures downstream accuracy across Pythia sizes, seeds, and checkpoints rather than fitting held-out-loss scaling laws or optimizing parameter/token allocations. It also reports seed-related training-loss spikes in two runs.
record.method_sensitivity: Downstream outcomes vary with task, model size, seed, and training checkpoint. The authors report a performance drop between steps 10^4 and 10^5 for all but 410M, especially in the smallest models; the two 410M outlier seeds show loss spikes.

fits_no_version.finding: Seeds 3 and 4 of the 410M model show training-loss spikes and final accuracy more than 2 SD below the other seeds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Same-configuration runs can produce seed-specific instabilities that break the expected per-size performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Probe macro-F1 improves with model size. Trajectories of representational metrics correlate across sizes (r = 0.99, 0.98 and 0.94), and training maps from smaller models predict 410M performance (R² > 0.9, except 14M).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training dynamics and representational quality of small models predict those of larger models.

record.problems: The paper limits its model-size sweep to 14M–410M parameters. Downstream accuracy values relevant here are presented in figures, with median and interquartile ranges across seeds but no numerical table. The study does not measure held-out pretraining loss for scaling fits or test loss extrapolation. The paper notes that a formal outlier test would require a larger sample of tasks.
record.rows_left_out: No directly relevant downstream-accuracy conditions or reported training-loss spike results were left out. Gender-bias, representation-probing, and training-map metrics were not included because they do not measure V6 downstream task performance or held-out pretraining-loss scaling.

untested.parts: No held-out-loss power-law fits in parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from small runs to larger ones.
No measurement of the loss-optimal split. The Chinchilla token count (8.2B) is only cited as a reference point for downstream accuracy.
No comparison of shapes at fixed parameter count.
Text pretraining only; no other modalities, repeated data or transfer.
No fitted predictive relation, no prediction of larger-model scores, and no link from downstream accuracy to pretraining loss. The size range is limited to 14M–410M.
No comparison of exponents or fitting choices.

missing.what: Accuracy drop between steps 10^4 and 10^5 for 14M–160M but not 410M ('saturation').
All benchmarks keep improving past the Chinchilla-optimal token count (8.2B tokens, about steps 4k–5k).
410M seeds 3 and 4 fall below the 2-SD band on final accuracy, giving larger performance variance across seeds (σ² 0.98 for 410M).

record.verdict_notes: This is a resource and stability paper, and scaling evidence is incidental. The per-size rows split what is really one across-size ordering claim, and all values are figure-only. The rows miss the time axis (saturation drop), which is the main V6-relevant nuance. The Chinchilla remark concerns downstream accuracy, not the loss optimum, so it does not test V3.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining-loss power laws in parameter count, tokens, or compute are not fitted or tested.
No power laws fitted on small runs are used to predict losses of larger runs.

The paper does not measure loss-minimising parameter and token allocations at fixed compute. It notes that benchmark scores continue to improve beyond the cited Chinchilla token count, but this is not a test of the stated loss-optimal split.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The study concerns text pretraining and does not test other modalities, repeated-data regimes, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling laws.
It reports descriptive downstream accuracy across sizes and checkpoints, but does not fit a predictive relationship, test extrapolation, or relate downstream performance to pretraining loss.
It does not compare loss-law exponents or compute-optimal splits across fitting or setup choices, nor test departures from fitted power laws.
